To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the pea chloroplast DNA atpH gene encodes a protein of 81 amino acids that is very similar to CFo subunit-III from other organisms; and (b) two abundant transcripts of 650 and 980 nucleotides were detected for the atpH gene.

the atpH gene of pea chloroplast DNA encodes the CFo subunit of ATP synthase and that the atpI-atpF-atpH region of the chloroplast DNA is transcribed in vivo to give large polycistronic transcripts and small, gene-specific transcripts.
The atpH transcript was processed at 5'-UGGAU, and the atpH gene was transcribed as a 660 nucleotide (nt) and a 980 nt transcript.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and expression of chloroplast genes in higher plants.
the molecular mechanisms of chloroplast gene expression and the role of RNA editing in chloroplasts.
the molecular biology of chloroplast gene expression and the role of the chloroplast in the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pea chloroplast ATP synthase is composed of 13 subunits, of which 11 are encoded by the chloroplast genome and two are encoded by the nuclear genome.

the 660 and 980 nt transcripts were both derived from the atpH gene and that the 980 nt transcripts represented the full-length transcript, which was processed at the 5'-end by endonucleolysis to produce the shorter 660 nt transcripts.
the atpH gene codes for subunit III of the chloroplast ATP synthase. [1]
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atpI gene is transcribed as a 2-kilobase pair RNA, the atpH gene as a 660-nt RNA, and the atpF gene as a 980-nt RNA.
the chloroplast atpF, atpH and atpI genes are cotranscribed, with the 660- and 980-nt transcripts being the major products.

the atpH gene encodes the CFo subunit of the chloroplast ATP synthase, that the atpI-atpH region contains a number of promoters, and that the 660 nt atpH transcripts may be derived from a primary transcript of 980 nt by processing at a conserved UGGAAU sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the atpH gene has a complex transcription pattern.
the atpH gene has been shown to be transcribed as part of the atpH-atpF-atpI operon in pea chloroplasts.
, in the context of the current literature, we are the first to show that a chloroplast-encoded CFo subunit is required for the assembly of CFo into the thylakoid membrane.
